summary.en: Sudanese armed forces carried out a drone strike on Abyei’s Amiet market, killing dozens and injuring many, prompting South Sudan to summon Sudan’s envoy over the attack. A separate drone strike in the disputed Sudan-South Sudan border region also caused high casualties. In Ruweng, fresh attacks left nine dead and six wounded, while in Northern Bahr el Ghazal bodies arrived from Khor Kaltan killings. Communal clashes continued, including 14 deaths between Warrap and Lakes communities and a traditional chief’s arrest over a Juba youth killing. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Den sudanske hæren utførte et droneangrep på Amiet-markedet i Abyei, der drepte dusinvis og såret mange, og fikk Sør-Sudan til å innkalle Sudans sendebud over angrepet. Et separat droneangrep i det omstridte grenseområdet mellom Sudan og Sør-Sudan forårsaket også høye tap. I Ruweng førte nye angrep til ni døde og seks sårede, mens i Nord-Bahr el Ghazal ankom lik fra drapene i Khor Kaltan. Kommunale sammenstøt fortsatte, inkludert 14 dødsfall mellom Warrap‑ og Lakes-samfunnene og arrestasjonen av en tradisjonell høvding over et drap på en ungdom i Juba. To dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir Mayardit and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
